# Adjudication Task — Chapter 710

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃710화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|느껴진다. 눈앞까지 드리운 죽음이.
  6|
  7|흐릿해진 시야는 사물의 형체조차 제대로 분간하지 못하고, 날카롭던 감각은 몸뚱어리를 떠날 준비를 끝마치고 있다.
  8|
  9|그 어둡고 몽롱한 의식 속에서, 진태경은 생각했다.
 10|
 11|틀림없다.
 12|
 13|이건 꿈이다. 아니면 가까워진 죽음과 함께 찾아온 환청이거나.
 14|
 15|그렇지 않고서야, 지금 등 뒤에서 들려오는 이 목소리를 설명할 방법이 없었다.
 16|
 17|“감히 누구의 몸에 손을 대려는 것이냐, 이 호로 잡년아.”
 18|
 19|그럼에도…… 닮았다.
 20|
 21|신경질적으로 들릴 만큼 카랑카랑한 목소리도, 저 걸쭉한 욕설도 한 사람을 떠올리게 만든다. 그런 일은 벌어지지 않을 거라는 사실을 아는데도. 말도 안 되는 생각이라 자책하면서도 헛된 희망을 품게 만든다.
 22|
 23|‘정말 죽을 때가 됐나.’
 24|
 25|공허한 뇌까림이 마음속에서 울려 퍼지던 그 순간.
 26|
 27|“그래서…… 네놈은 언제까지 그리 넋 놓고 있을 셈이냐?”
 28|
 29|“……!”
 30|
 31|스르륵 감기려던 진태경의 눈꺼풀이 우뚝 멈췄다.
 32|
 33|찰나 지간 찾아온 거대한 충격에 닫혀 가던 정신이 깨어나고, 멀어진 감각들이 돌아온다.
 34|
 35|‘설마.’
 36|
 37|아니다. 아닐 것이다.
 38|
 39|그건 있을 수 없는 일이니까. ‘그’는 머나먼 중원 어딘가에 있어야 할 사람이었으니까.
 40|
 41|하지만 누군가 그랬다.
 42|
 43|인간을 무너트리는 것도, 다시 일으켜 세우는 것도 결국 희망이라고. 그렇기에 진태경은 보이지 않는 희망의 끈을 붙잡으며 눈을 떴다.
 44|
 45|그리고 볼 수 있었다.
 46|
 47|“아. 아아…….”
 48|
 49|양팔을 모두 잃은 채, 신형을 비틀거리는 남천마후의 모습을.
 50|
 51|그리고 경악과 의문에 사로잡힌 그녀의 옆에 비스듬히 꽂혀 있는 한 자루의 선장(禪杖)을.
 52|
 53|쩔그럭.
 54|
 55|선장에 매달린 고리가 요란한 소리를 토해 낸다.
 56|
 57|불그스름하게 달아오른 그것으로부터 흘러나온 열양지기(熱陽之氣)를 느낀 진태경이 흐릿한 미소와 함께 입을 열었다.
 58|
 59|“거…… 일찍 좀 오시지.”
 60|
 61|바로 옆에서 귀를 기울여야만 들을 수 있을 만큼 희미한 목소리.
 62|
 63|그러나 선장의 주인은 달랐다.
 64|
 65|그는 수백여 장 밖이어도, 아니 설령 수백 리를 떨어져 있다 하더라도 진태경의 목소리를 들을 수 있을 것이다.
 66|
 67|귀가 아닌 마음으로.
 68|
 69|하나뿐인 제자를 향한 마음으로.
 70|
 71|“좀 늦을 수도 있지, 어린놈이 구박은.”
 72|
 73|마음과는 달리 퉁명스럽게 대답한 혈승(血僧), 아니 화왕(火王) 적천강이 걸음을 내디뎠다.
 74|
 75|저벅.
 76|
 77|그리고 다음 순간.
 78|
 79|화륵.
 80|
 81|모든 무대가 끝나고 찾아온 암전(暗轉) 속에서, 그 어떤 것보다 크고 맹렬한 불꽃이 솟구쳤다.
 82|
 83|콰아아아아!
 84|
 85|화염신장(火焰神掌).
 86|
 87|끔찍한 열기를 머금은 불길의 파도가 어둠을 살라 먹으며 나아간다. 거침없으며 끝없이, 오직 한 존재를 불태우기 위해서.
 88|
 89|‘아.’
 90|
 91|남천마후는 텅 빈 눈으로 다가오는 열기를 바라보았다.
 92|
 93|외마디 신음도, 비명도 입 밖으로 흘러나오지 않는다. 발은 못 박힌 것처럼 지면에 고정되어 있었고, 양팔의 고통은 멀게만 느껴졌다.
 94|
 95|‘피해야 하는데. 어떻게든 피해야 하는데…….’
 96|
 97|머리에서 계속되는 외침을 몸이 받아들이지 못한다.
 98|
 99|아니, 어쩌면 하나뿐이었던 팔을 잃은 그 순간 모든 것이 끝났을지도 모른다.
100|
101|섬광이라 착각할 만큼 빠르고, 강대한 열기를 머금고 있던 한 자루의 선장이 잿가루로 만든 것은 그녀의 팔뿐만이 아니다.
102|
103|선천지기(先天之氣).
104|
105|오직 한 사람의 최후를 장식하기 위하여 남겨 두었던 그 마지막 한 줌의 힘마저 앗아 가 버렸다. 무심히, 그리고 무참히.
106|
107|이제는 한 걸음 내뻗을 힘조차 남아 있지 않은 자신을 관조하며, 남천마후는 비로소 깨달았다.
108|
109|‘끝이구나.’
110|
111|실로 길었던 인생. 그 시작이 정확히 어디쯤이었는지는 모르겠으나, 오늘 이 자리가 그녀의 마침표일 것이다.
112|
113|그럼에도 마지막까지 남은 후회가 있다면, 그것은 진태경의 숨통을 직접 끊어 놓지 못한 것에 대한 아쉬움뿐이리라.
114|
115|‘하지만…… 괜찮아.’
116|
117|왜, 어떤 운명의 장난으로 화왕 적천강이 이곳에 왔는지는 모른다.
118|
119|그러나 자신이 이곳에서 쓰러지는 것처럼, 진태경 역시 죽음을 피할 수 없을 것이다.
120|
121|설령 화왕이 아니라 대라신선(大羅神仙)이 온다 해도 그 사실은 변치 않는다.
122|
123|이 흔들리지 않을 한 가지 확신이, 불길을 받아들이는 남천마후의 마음을 편안케 했다.
124|
125|‘천주시여.’
126|
127|마음속에서 나지막하게 울려 퍼지는 부름.
128|
129|상념은 길었으나 순간은 짧았고, 무릎 꿇은 진태경의 머리 위로 쏘아진 불꽃은 남천마후를 향해 아가리를 벌렸다.
130|
131|화아아악!
132|
133|어둠을 녹이며 쏟아지는 광염(光焰)을 바라보며, 남천마후는 눈을 감았다.
134|
135|아니, 눈을 감으려 했다.
136|
137|모든 것이 새하얗게 물들던 그때, 손 하나 까딱할 힘조차 남아 있지 않은 몸뚱어리를 덮치는 누군가의 신형이 아니었다면 그러했을 것이다.
138|
139|와락!
140|
141|찰나를 쪼개고 쪼갠 짧은 순간 속, 남천마후는 똑똑히 볼 수 있었다.
142|
143|“……!”
144|
145|죽음을 앞두고 창백하게 질린 진태경의 얼굴과, 느려진 세상 속에서 서서히 벌어지는 그의 입술을.
146|
147|그리고.
148|
149|콰득!
150|
151|목으로부터 전해지는 아릿한 고통과 함께, 남천마후의 시야가 어둠으로 물들었다.
152|
153|
154|
155|* * *
156|
157|
158|
159|그것은 피할 수 없는 현실인 동시에, 섬광과도 같은 깨달음이었다.
160|
161|‘지금 남천마후가 죽으면, 나도 죽는다.’
162|
163|지금까지 나보다 윗줄의 강자들과 맞붙으면서도 살아남을 수 있었던 가장 큰 이유는, 레벨 업으로 말미암은 회복 덕분이었다.
164|
165|제아무리 근골이 뛰어나고 여러 능력치를 높여 놔도 확실한 죽음만큼은 막지 못한다.
166|
167|지금의 나처럼 혈도가 박살 나고, 원위치에서 올바른 기능을 수행해야 할 십이지장이 휴가 나온 군인처럼 위수 지역을 벗어난 경우에는 더더욱 그렇다.
168|
169|그런데 이런 상황에서 남천마후가 내가 아닌 다른 사람의 손에 죽는다?
170|
171|그럼 나까지 좆 되는 거다.
172|
173|결국, 마지막 순간 내게 주어진 선택지는 하나뿐이었다.
174|
175|몸빵.
176|
177|‘시발.’
178|
179|나직한 욕설을 삼키며, 나는 젖먹던 힘까지 쥐어 짜내어 몸을 튕겼다.
180|
181|아니, 간신히 몸을 일으켜 남천마후의 신형을 덮쳤다고 하는 것이 더 옳은 표현일 것이다.
182|
183|와락!
184|
185|“……!”
186|
187|체념한 듯 감겨가던 눈이 부릅떠지는 것이 보였다.
188|
189|경악과 의문. 두 가지 감정이 소용돌이치는 남천마후의 눈동자가 목소리를 대신하여 묻는 듯했다.
190|
191|도대체 왜?
192|
193|하지만 대답해 줄 이유도, 그럴 만한 시간도 없다.
194|
195|그 정도의 여유와 힘이 남아 있었다면 몇 걸음 뒤에 떨어진 백염을 주웠거나, 인벤토리에서 다른 무기를 꺼내 남천마후의 심장에 박아 넣었을 것이다.
196|
197|그런데…… 빌어먹을. 당장이라도 끊어질 것 같은 정신을 붙잡으며 할 수 있는 최선의 공격이라곤, 결국 이것뿐이다.
198|
199|콰득!
200|
201|검버섯이 핀 주름진 피부가 힘없이 뜯겨 나간다. 비릿한 핏물이 입안을 가득 채우고, 바싹 마른 입술을 축축하게 적셨다.
202|
203|지금까지 겪은 모든 전투를 통틀어, 가장 원초적이며 원시적인 공격. 그렇기에 어느 때보다 간절했던 일격.
204|
205|그리고 남천마후의 목울대를 한입 가득 물어뜯은 나는, 다음 순간 등 뒤로 전해지는 어마어마한 열기를 느꼈다.
206|
207|비명과도 같은 누군가의 외침도 함께.
208|
209|“안-!”
210|
211|화륵, 퍼어어엉!
212|
213|등줄기를 강타하는 엄청난 충격. 이어지려던 외침마저 집어삼킨 굉음이 끔찍한 열기와 함께 사방을 휩쓸었고, 나는 붕 뜬 듯한 부유감(浮游感)을 느끼며 튕겨 나갔다.
214|
215|‘아.’
216|
217|누가 그랬던가. 인간이 느낄 수 있는 통증 중 가장 큰 고통은, 불에 의한 작열통(灼熱痛)이라고.
218|
219|그리고 그 말은 틀림없는 사실이었다.
220|
221|비명조차 새어 나올 수 없는 끔찍한 고통이 전신을 사로잡는다.
222|
223|새하얗게 물든 시야는 한 치 앞도 분간할 수 없었고, 거대한 충격을 이기지 못하고 튕겨 나간 몸뚱어리는 그저 맹렬한 속도로 바람을 가를 뿐이었다.
224|
225|쐐애애애액, 콰앙!
226|
227|영원히 계속될 것만 같던 세찬 파공성이 끝나고, 거칠고 단단한 무언가가 전신을 후려친다.
228|
229|아니, 빛살처럼 쏘아진 내 몸이 잔해를 부수며 틀어박혔다고 하는 것이 옳았다.
230|
231|쿨럭.
232|
233|발은 기침과 함께 이제 얼마 남지도 않았을 핏물이 입가를 타고 흘러나온다.
234|
235|이미 터져 나간 고막에서는 벌 떼 우는 소리가 요란하고, 흐릿한 시야 너머에서는 힘없이 널브러진 남천마후의 모습과 누군가의 인영이 아지랑이처럼 일렁이고 있었다.
236|
237|“안 돼-!”
238|
239|그리고, 비명과도 같은 외침이 울려 퍼진 그 순간.
240|
241|띠링.
242|
243|귓가를 파고드는 맑은 종소리와 함께, 따스한 온기가 나를 감싸 안았다.
244|
245|
246|
247|* * *
248|
249|
250|
251|쐐애애액!
252|
253|지금 이 순간. 전력을 다해 신형을 내딛는 적천강의 마음은 절망으로 가득했다.
254|
255|‘안 돼. 안 된다.’
256|
257|한 걸음, 한 걸음이 무겁다.
258|
259|백 년이 넘는 세월을 살아오며 늙어 버린 가슴은 그 어느 때보다 가파르게 요동쳤고, 빠르게 가까워지는 한 사람에게 못 박힌 눈동자는 파르르 떨리고 있었다.
260|
261|진태경.
262|
263|그의 생애 두 번째이자, 하나뿐인 제자.
264|
265|그리고 죽음만을 바라던 자신에게 어느 날 문득 찾아와, 살아가야 할 이유를 깨닫게 해 주었던 유일한 불씨.
266|
267|‘그런데. 그런데 도대체 왜!’
268|
269|당장이라도 피를 토할 것만 같은 심정이었다.
270|
271|그가 남천마후를 향해 쏘아 보냈던 것은 자그마치 십이성(十二成)의 경지에 이른 화염신장이다.
272|
273|한데 강철마저 녹여 버리는 그 끔찍한 열기를, 난데없이 진태경이 막아선 것이다.
274|
275|‘이 미친놈. 멍청한 놈 같으니!’
276|
277|이유는 모른다. 아니, 이유 따윈 중요하지 않았다. 미처 토해 내지 못한 욕설 역시 적천강 자신을 향한 것이었다.
278|
279|진태경의, 하나뿐인 제자의 선택은 언제나 옳았고 그만한 이유가 있었으니까.
280|
281|그저 자신의 성급한 판단으로 진태경을 잃게 되었다는 슬픔과 자책만이 적천강의 마음을 갈기갈기 찢어 놓았다.
282|
283|“안 돼!”
284|
285|비명과도 같은 외침과 함께, 늙은 스승의 발걸음이 마침내 제자의 앞에서 멈추었다.
286|
287|“태경아! 이놈아!”
288|

*Fuck.*

Whump!

*Why?*

[P85]

[P86]

[P87]
Crack!

[P89]

[P90]

“No—!”

*Ah.*

They were right.

[P98]

[P99]
Screeeeeech—boom!

[P117]

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

Whoosh!

Kraaaaaash!

*Ah.*

*I have to dodge. Somehow…*

Her innate qi.

*It’s over.*

*Lord of Heaven.*

[P58]
Whoooosh!

Whump!

Whump!

“……!”

*Why?*

[P87]
Crack!

[P89]

“No—!”

Whoosh! Boom!

[P95]
*Ah.*

[P96]

[P97]

[P98]

[P99]
Screeeeeech—boom!

Cough.

[P103]

“No!”

[P106]
At that scream—

[P107]
Ding.

[P108]
A clear bell rang in my ear, and warmth enveloped me.

[P109]
* * *

[P110]
Screeeeeech!

[P111]

[P112]
*No. No, this can’t happen.*

[P113]
Every step felt heavy.

[P114]
His heart, aged by more than a century, pounded harder than it ever had. His eyes trembled, fixed on the person rapidly drawing closer.

[P115]
Jin Taekyung.

[P116]
The second Disciple he had taken in his lifetime, and the only one he had left.

[P117]
The one ember that had appeared in the life of a man who had wished only for death and shown him a reason to keep living.

[P118]
*Then why? Why the hell—*

[P119]
He felt as though he might cough up blood.

[P120]

[P121]
And Taekyung had leaped in front of it.

[P122]
*You crazy bastard. You stupid bastard!*

[P123]
Jeok Cheongang did not know why. The reason did not matter. The curses he could not bring himself to shout were meant for himself.

[P124]

[P125]
It was the grief and guilt of knowing his own hasty judgment had cost Taekyung his life that tore Jeok Cheongang’s heart apart.

[P126]
“No!”

[P127]
The old master’s desperate cry rang out as he finally stopped before his Disciple.

[P128]
“Taekyung! You bastard!”

[P129]
There was no answer.

[P130]
Taekyung lay with his eyes closed, his breathing so faint it could stop at any moment. Jeok Cheongang’s heart sank.

[P131]
*Ah.*

[P132]
His vision swam.

[P133]
Taekyung’s armor was shattered beyond recognition. His limbs lay twisted at unnatural angles. Beneath the heat of the Flame Divine Palm, flesh had melted and bone had broken.

[P134]
Perhaps the armor had saved him. Somehow, he was still breathing.

[P135]
But only just. He had mere moments left.

[P136]
Even if Jeok Cheongang poured all his internal energy into him, it would not change that. It would only prolong the pain.

Tap.

[P139]

[P140]

[P141]

[P142]

[P143]

[P144]

[P145]

[P146]

[P149]

[P150]

[P151]
“……?”

[P153]
*What the hell?*

[P154]

[P155]
Gulp.

[P157]
A pair of eyes was watching him with interest.

[P158]
“……?”

[P159]
“……?”

[P160]
“……!”

[P161]
“……!”

[P163]

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.

Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

[P85]
If I’d had the strength, I would have picked up White Flame from where it had fallen a few steps away. Or pulled another weapon from my Inventory and driven it into her heart.

[P86]
But damn it, I could barely hold on to consciousness. This was the best attack I had left.

[P87]
Crack!

[P88]
Wrinkled skin mottled with age spots tore away. The taste of blood filled my mouth and wet my parched lips.

[P89]
Of all the attacks I’d made in all the battles I’d fought, this was the most primitive. And I had never needed one to work more badly.

[P90]
I tore a mouthful from the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s throat.

[P91]
Then I felt tremendous heat at my back and heard someone scream.

[P92]
“No—!”

[P93]
Whoosh! Boom!

[P94]
A massive impact slammed into me. A roar swallowed the rest of the cry, and terrible heat swept out in every direction. I felt weightless for an instant before it hurled me away.

[P95]
*Ah.*

[P96]
Who was it who said that the worst pain a person could feel was being burned?

[P97]
They were right.

[P98]
Pain too awful to scream through seized my entire body. My vision went white. I couldn’t see an inch in front of me as I hurtled through the air.

[P99]
Screeeeeech—boom!

[P100]
The rushing wind seemed to go on forever. Then something rough and hard struck my whole body.

[P101]
No. My body had shot through the rubble like a beam of light and buried itself there.

[P102]
Cough.

[P103]
What little blood I had left trickled from the corner of my mouth.

[P104]
My eardrums had burst, yet I heard a swarm of bees buzzing in my ears. Through my blurred vision, I could make out the Southern Heaven Demon Empress sprawled on the ground and someone’s figure wavering like a heat haze.

[P105]
“No!”

[P106]
At that scream—

[P107]
Ding.

[P108]
A clear bell rang in my ear, and warmth enveloped me.

[P109]
* * *

[P110]
Screeeeeech!

[P111]
Jeok Cheongang raced forward with all his strength, his heart full of despair.

[P112]
*No. No, this can’t happen.*

[P113]
Every step felt heavy.

[P114]
His heart, aged by more than a century, pounded harder than it ever had. His eyes trembled, fixed on the person rapidly drawing closer.

[P115]
Jin Taekyung.

[P116]
The second Disciple he had taken in his lifetime, and the only one he had left.

[P117]
The one ember that had appeared in the life of a man who had wished only for death and shown him a reason to keep living.

[P118]
*Then why? Why the hell—*

[P119]
He felt as though he might cough up blood.

[P120]
He had unleashed the Flame Divine Palm at the twelve-star stage of mastery upon the Southern Heaven Demon Empress. It carried heat fierce enough to melt steel.

[P121]
And Taekyung had leaped in front of it.

[P122]
*You crazy bastard. You stupid bastard!*

[P123]

[P124]
His one and only Disciple had always had a reason for his choices. He had always been right.

[P125]
It was the grief and guilt of knowing his own hasty judgment had cost Taekyung his life that tore Jeok Cheongang’s heart apart.

[P126]
“No!”

[P127]

[P128]
“Taekyung! You bastard!”

[P129]
There was no answer.

[P130]

[P131]
*Ah.*

[P132]
His vision swam.

[P133]

[P134]
Perhaps the armor had saved him. Somehow, he was still breathing.

[P135]
But only just. He had mere moments left.

[P136]
Even if Jeok Cheongang poured all his internal energy into him, it would not change that. It would only prolong the pain.

[P137]
Tap.

[P138]

[P139]
*…Dying? He’s dying? That boy?*

[P140]

[P141]

[P142]
But Taekyung was different.

[P143]

[P144]
“What… what could be so urgent that you have to leave already? Why!”

[P145]

[P146]

[P147]
*Huh?*

[P148]

[P149]
Through his tears, he saw Taekyung’s hand.

[P150]
The back of it was pale and smooth as a newborn baby’s. Its veins stood out in thick ridges.

[P151]
“……?”

[P152]

[P153]
*What the hell?*

[P154]
There were only two possibilities. Either those damned infirmities of old age had returned, or…

[P155]
Gulp.

[P156]
Jeok Cheongang swallowed and slowly raised his head.

[P157]
A pair of eyes was watching him with interest.

[P158]
“……?”

[P159]
“……?”

[P160]
“……!”

[P161]
“……!”

[P162]

[P163]
Taekyung wiggled his fingers sheepishly.

[P164]
“Um, could you let go of my hand first? Then we can talk.”

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
